newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SEA HARVEST CAUTIONS ON FISHING RESTRUCTURE.
newsitem.headline: SEA HARVEST CAUTIONS ON FISHING RESTRUCTURE.

text.p: Any restructuring of the ownership of South Africa's fishing industry to accommodate black interests should aim to minimise disruption, Sea Harvest Corporation Ltd chairman Eckardt Kramer said.
In his latest annual report, Kramer said although there had been much agreement in the debate on government's new fisheries policy, areas of discord remained.

"What has remained controversial, however, is the challenge on how to restructure the fishing industry to accommodate persons or groups who were previously disadvantaged without major disruption of the industry," he said.
Kramer said the best way of increasing black participation would be through employee share ownership schemes.

Sea Harvest had launched such a scheme, in terms of which every employee was offered shares at a discount to the market price. Kramer said 2,470 employees had taken up the offer and 1.2 million shares were issued to them.
Further shares would be offered which would result in a short-term dilution of earnings per share by about five percent.
"(But) the benefits of direct employee participation in the success of the group will have long term positive implications," Kramer said.
Furthermore, he said the group planned to invest 32 million rand in modernising its shipping fleet and processing facilities this year.
It was expected that markets would remain firm in the coming year and that real earnings growth could be expected if catch rates in South Africa and Namibia were satisfactory.
